MHC II combined immunodeficiency; recurrent infections are separate diseases. Diarrhea alone and sparse neurologic observations do not establish common direct organ damage.
Familial focal epilepsy, with cortical dysplasia reported in 1/2 patients, is a nervous system disorder.

Defined by increased neonatal red blood cell concentration; other organ complications are not defining or consistently common.
Perlecan disorders encompass skeletal dysplasia and Schwartz-Jampel neuromuscular hyperexcitability; additional organ damage is not shared across the group.
Cutaneous ectoparasitic infestation; tick paralysis is a minority subtype rather than a shared manifestation.
Defined by cerebral ventriculomegaly and cystic kidney disease, each documented in 4/6 patients; cardiac abnormalities are uncommon.
Carcinoma originates in the urinary bladder, which belongs to the renal axis.
Cerebellar and extrapyramidal degeneration with cognitive impairment; abnormal eye movements reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than ocular damage.
Systemic opportunistic fungal infection; no particular organ is consistently affected across the included mycoses.
Dandy-Walker malformation, intellectual disability, severe myopia and brachytelephalangy define it; dental and palatal abnormalities occur in 80-99%.
B-cell lymphoma with cellular immunodeficiency; extranodal organ damage is uncommon, and cough or pruritus alone does not establish damage.
Defined by vascular malformations; cutaneous vessel involvement does not independently establish skin tissue damage across the spectrum.
Spinal ligament ossification directly compresses cord or roots; myelopathy affects roughly 30-50% over the course. Associated diabetes is separate.
Hypertension defines this cardiovascular disease; chemotherapy is its cause, not an additional organ manifestation.
MTOR overgrowth disorders commonly feature megalencephaly, cortical abnormalities and neurodevelopmental dysfunction; extracerebral involvement varies.
Sarcoma originates in the vulva, a reproductive organ outside the axes; mesenchymal histology alone does not establish locomotor involvement.
Cervical vertebral dysplasia, facet hypoplasia and atlanto-occipital instability define a skeletal disorder; neurologic damage is not established.
Partial gp130 deficiency causes combined immunodeficiency; skeletal abnormalities including craniosynostosis and eczema are common (about 30% or more).
Congenital eyelid abnormalities and dental agenesis define the syndrome; cleft lip affects 2/3. Cutaneous syndactyly is very rare.
Germ cell tumor originates in the brain; endocrine dysfunction depends on tumor location and is not established as common across this concept.
Defined as isolated multiple cafe-au-lait macules without neurofibromatosis or another systemic disorder.
Axonal peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy; distal muscle wasting and weakness result from denervation rather than direct muscle disease.
